questions.stem: What is the result of a neutralisation reaction?
questions.solution: A neutralisation reaction results in salt and water. Acids and bases react to form these products, as the hydrogen ions from the acid combine with hydroxide ions from the base to create water, while the remaining ions form a salt. Heat is often released, but it is a byproduct, not the main result. Acid and base are the starting materials, not the products, and gas is not typically produced in a neutralisation reaction.

hi.stem: एक उदासीनीकरण अभिक्रिया का परिणाम क्या होता है?
hi.solution: एक उदासीनीकरण अभिक्रिया लवण और पानी के परिणाम के रूप में होती है। अम्ल और क्षार एक दूसरे से अभिक्रिया करके इन उत्पादों का निर्माण करते हैं, क्योंकि अम्ल से हाइड्रोजन आयन क्षार से हाइड्रॉक्साइड आयन के साथ मिलकर पानी बनाते हैं, जबकि शेष आयन एक लवण बनाते हैं। ऊष्मा अक्सर उत्पन्न होती है, लेकिन यह एक उत्पाद नहीं है, बल्कि एक अपकर्ष है। अम्ल और क्षार शुरू के सामग्री हैं, उत्पाद नहीं, और उदासीनीकरण अभिक्रिया में गैस आमतौर पर उत्पन्न नहीं होती है।
hi.critique: The Hindi translation is accurate, maintains the original meaning, and uses standard scientific terminology appropriate for Hindi-medium textbooks.

questions.stem: Which of the following groups contains only acidic substances?
choices: Lime water, baking soda solution, salt solution
Tap water, sugar solution, washing powder solution
questions.solution: Lemon juice, vinegar, and tamarind water are all acidic and turn blue litmus paper red. Soap solution and lime water are basic, while tap water, sugar solution, and washing powder solution are neutral.

questions.stem: In which of the following situations is a base used to neutralise an acid?
choices: Applying lemon juice to a wound
Using baking soda to treat an ant bite
questions.solution: Baking soda is a base that can neutralise the formic acid injected by an ant, which is a common example of a neutralisation reaction. Lemon juice is acidic and would not neutralise an acid. Spraying water does not involve a chemical reaction, and adding salt does not neutralise an acid.

hi.stem: निम्नलिखित में से किस स्थिति में एसिड को उदासीन करने के लिए क्षार का उपयोग किया जाता है?

questions.stem: What is the purpose of adding lime to acidic soil?
choices: To increase the acidity of the soil
To neutralise the acidity of the soil
To reduce the moisture content of the soil
To increase the nutrient content of the soil
questions.solution: Lime is added to neutralise the acidity of the soil because it is a base that reacts with acids, balancing the pH level. This makes the soil more suitable for plant growth. Increasing acidity or reducing moisture are not effects of lime, and while lime may indirectly affect nutrients, its main purpose is not to increase them.

मिट्टी के पोषक तत्वों के स्तर को बढ़ाना
hi.solution: चूना अम्लीय मिट्टी के अम्लता को उदासीन करने के लिए डाला जाता है क्योंकि यह एक क्षार है जो अम्लों के साथ अभिक्रिया करता है, जिससे pH स्तर संतुलित हो जाता है। इससे मिट्टी पौधों के लिए अधिक उपयुक्त हो जाती है। अम्लता बढ़ाना या नमी कम करना चूने के प्रभाव नहीं हैं, और यद्यपि चूना पोषक तत्वों पर अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से प्रभाव डाल सकता है, इसका मुख्य उद्देश्य उन्हें बढ़ाना नहीं है।

questions.stem: Which of the following solutions would have the highest pH value?
questions.solution: Sodium hydroxide is a strong base and has the highest pH value. Sulphuric acid is a strong acid, acetic acid is a weak acid, and magnesium hydroxide is a weak base.

hi.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा विलयन सबसे अधिक pH मान रखेगा?

hi.critique: Translation is accurate and maintains the original meaning, technical terms are appropriately translated for Hindi-medium curriculum.

questions.stem: A student added a few drops of lemon juice to a solution and observed that the solution turned red. What could the solution be?
questions.solution: The solution could be blue litmus solution because blue litmus turns red in acidic conditions, and lemon juice is acidic. Turmeric does not change color in acidic solutions, baking soda is a base and would not react this way, and phenolphthalein turns pink in basic solutions, not red.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the use of natural indicators like red rose extract and turmeric paper?
choices: They are more accurate than synthetic indicators
They can distinguish between acidic and neutral substances
They can only be used in laboratory settings
They are not reliable for identifying the strength of acids and bases

questions.stem: Why does the message written with a solution become visible when another solution is sprayed on it?
choices: Because the second solution is acidic
Because the second solution is basic
Because the two solutions form a salt
Because the two solutions react to change the color
questions.solution: The message becomes visible because the two solutions react chemically, causing a color change. The correct option highlights this reaction, which is the direct cause of the visibility. The other options focus on properties like acidity or basicity, which may influence the reaction but are not the reason for the color change itself. Forming a salt is a byproduct, not the primary reason for the visibility.

hi.solution: संदेश दिखाई देने के कारण दोनों विलयनों की रासायनिक अभिक्रिया होती है जिसके कारण रंग बदल जाता है। सही विकल्प इस अभिक्रिया को दर्शाता है जो दृश्यता के सीधा कारण है। अन्य विकल्प अम्लीयता या क्षारीयता जैसे गुणों पर ध्यान केंद्रित करते हैं, जो अभिक्रिया को प्रभावित कर सकते हैं लेकिन रंग परिवर्तन के कारण नहीं हैं। लवण बनाना एक उप उत्पाद है, जो दृश्यता के प्राथमिक कारण नहीं है।
